articles.headline: FA: Man City verdict has 'significant implications for integrity of game'
articles.description: The Football Association have expressed their concern that the guilty charge aimed at Manchester City over the Premier League's financial rules stains the "integrity" of the game.
articles.headlineJa: FA：マンチェスター・シティ裁定は「競技の公平性に重大な影響を及ぼす」
articles.descriptionJa: イングランドサッカー協会（FA）は、プレミアリーグの財務ルール違反を巡るマンチェスター・シティへの有罪判定が競技の「公平性」を損なうとして懸念を表明しました。
articles.body:
The Football Association have expressed their concern that the guilty charge aimed at Manchester City over the Premier League's financial rules stains the "integrity" of the game.

The FA's full statement read: "The Independent Commission's decision has significant implications for the integrity of the game. We are carefully considering the decision and its implications and will take action where appropriate.

"As proceedings between the Premier League and Manchester City Football Club remain ongoing, we do not intend to comment further at this stage. We will, however, continue to monitor developments closely."

Friday, Oct. 2 is the deadline for City to appeal the guilty verdict into their breaches of Premier League rules. They have stated that they intend to appeal.

The commission concluded more than £830 million ($1.1 bn) of such funding was used to inflate revenues and enable the club to comply with Premier League and UEFA financial rules through a series of "sham" arrangements.

At the heart of the club's appeal will be an insistence that government funding, provided via the Abu Dhabi Crown Prince Court (CPC), gave financial assistance to sponsors in the emirate to help them to fulfil their liabilities to City, rather than Sheikh Mansour's Abu Dhabi United Group (ADUG) company, which owns the club.

The 40-page core decision published on Tuesday shows the independent commission rejected the CPC explanation as "untrue" in its findings, adding: "We concluded that it was an 'explanation' that the club had concocted well after the event in an attempt to obscure and conceal the realities of the disguised funding scheme."

Sponsor Etihad Airways, which is owned by an Abu Dhabi fund chaired by City owner Sheikh Mansour's brother, is considering legal action against the Premier League.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham told the BBC earlier this week that he would be concerned if City's owners sold the club due to the guilty verdict because they have been "a huge partner in the building of modern Manchester." But a No. 10 Downing Street spokesman afterwards: "As the Prime Minister made clear, the initial judgement is serious and there can't be any suggestion that anyone is above the rules.

"He also stressed that it is an ongoing independent process. It is essential that it is allowed to run its course and the outcome respected.

"If wrongdoing is established, those responsible should face the appropriate consequences."

But Jamie Carragher wrote for The Telegraph: "The club can only heal and recover from the shame of their guilt once the custodians recognise they have failed in their duty and sell up."

articles.headline: Sir Alex Ferguson was 'terrified' about Old Trafford return after brain surgery
articles.description: Sir Alex Ferguson has revealed he was "terrified" when returning to Old Trafford for the first time following brain surgery in 2018.
articles.headlineJa: アレックス・ファーガソン卿、脳手術後のオールド・トラッフォード復帰に「恐怖を感じていた」
articles.descriptionJa: アレックス・ファーガソン卿は、2018年に脳手術を受けてから初めてオールド・トラッフォードへ復帰した際、「恐怖を感じていた」と明かしました。
articles.body:
Sir Alex Ferguson has revealed he was "terrified" when returning to Old Trafford for the first time following brain surgery in 2018.

The former Manchester United manager, now 84, suffered a brain haemorrhage at the age of 76 and returned to the stadium four months later to watch them play Wolves in the Premier League.

"I was terrified actually," Ferguson told BBC Breakfast. "I wish I could say I was comfortable. I wasn't."

Ferguson and late wife Cathy were given a standing ovation when taking their seats in the directors' box.

"My wife was with me, and she was nearly crying," Ferguson said. "When we sat down, she said, 'that's fantastic.'"

Ferguson had retired as United boss five years before his brain haemorrhage, having won 36 major trophies during his 26-year spell in charge.

He also spoke about his fear after being left unable to talk in the days following his surgery.

"I had lost my voice. I couldn't speak," he said. "That was a frightening moment. I remember my grandsons coming to see me and I had lost my voice.

"Then they brought in a therapist and she started doing things like asking me to write down the names of birds, names of animals, names of rivers. That way my voice came back."

- Portugal, Man United, Real Madrid: Cristiano Ronaldo's long history of rows with coaches

- Transfer rumors, news: Man United, Chelsea monitoring Benfica defender

- FA charges Fulham boss Álvaro Arbeloa with misconduct for comments after Man United draw

When asked about his health now, he added: "I'm feeling quite good despite small injuries."

Ferguson has a new book in the pipeline, 'Games of My Life', in which he recalls the 21 matches he feels defined his career.

His unrivalled trophy haul at Old Trafford included 13 Premier League titles, two Champions Leagues, five FA Cups, four League Cups and the European Cup Winners' Cup.

articles.headline: 2026 Ballon d'Or: Full men's, women's short lists, host city change, more
articles.description: The 2026 Ballon d'Or short lists are out. Here's who could win the biggest individual prizes in men's and women's soccer.
articles.headlineJa: 2026年バロンドール：男女の最終候補全リスト、開催都市の変更など
articles.descriptionJa: 2026年バロンドールの最終候補リストが発表されました。男女サッカー界における最高の個人賞を獲得する可能性がある候補者たちを紹介します。
articles.body:
It's nearly that time again.

The 2026 Ballon d'Or awards -- the annual ceremony in which France Football Magazine crowns the best men's and women's players in the world -- are fast approaching, with the short list for each award announced on Tuesday.

The Ballon d'Or trophies are handed out based on the criteria of: "1) Individual performances, decisive and impressive character, 2) Team performances and achievements, 3) Class and fair play."

Any player in world football is eligible, no matter the league they play in or their country of origin, and the short lists are decided by a jury of 100 journalists from around the world. So who is nominated for this year's awards, and who could win?

When is the 2026 Ballon d'Or ceremony, and why isn't it in Paris?

The 2026 Ballon d'Or awards, which have long been presented by France Football Magazine, will be handed out on Oct. 26. There will be a difference this year, though: The star-studded ceremony will not take place in Paris. Instead, it will be held in London at The London Palladium theater to mark the gala's 70th anniversary.

The first Ballon d'Or ceremony was a much more humble affair, held in Blackpool, England, and awarded to 41-year-old star forward Stanley Matthews.

Matthews was an all-time England great who spent the majority of his career at Blackpool and Stoke City and, when announcing the venue change, was described by organizers as a "true ambassador of football."

"As the Ballon d'Or becomes of septuagenarian age, it is fitting in such a landmark year to celebrate the finest present-day exponents of the beautiful game in the beating heart of the country that first conceived of it," organizers added.

Full 30-player Ballon d'Or short list

Jude Bellingham

Club: Real Madrid

Country: England

Bellingham didn't win a trophy with Real Madrid for the second year running, but the all-action midfielder was an important pillar of England's bronze medal-winning display at the 2026 World Cup. The 23-year-old scored seven goals at the tournament and his virtuoso two-goal display against Mexico in the round of 16 is likely to go down in Three Lions' folklore.

 Pau Cubarsí

Club: Barcelona

Country: Spain

A debut nomination for 19-year-old center back Cubarsi, who played an important role in Barcelona's 2025-26 title win before being crowned Best Young Player at the World Cup after playing every single minute of Spain's monumental victory, keeping seven clean sheets along the way. He is also nominated for the Kopa Trophy, which is awarded to the best player aged 21 or younger.

 Marc Cucurella

Club: Chelsea / Real Madrid

Country: Spain

Cucurella was a mainstay for Chelsea in the Premier League in 2025-26 before completing a transfer to Real Madrid during the World Cup. The energetic left back played every single minute for Spain at the tournament, and even provided two assists before ending his summer as a world champion.

 Ousmane Dembélé

Club: Paris Saint-Germain

Country: France

articles.headline: Watson leads third straight winning drive, puts Browns atop North
articles.description: Deshaun Watson has the Browns atop the division at 3-1 after directing a winning drive for the third straight game Thursday night in a 27-24 win over the Steelers.
articles.headlineJa: ワトソンが3試合連続の決勝ドライブを導き、ブラウンズを北地区首位に押し上げる
articles.descriptionJa: デショーン・ワトソンが木曜夜に行われたスティーラーズ戦（27-24）で3試合連続となる決勝ドライブを指揮し、ブラウンズを3勝1敗で地区首位に立たせた。
articles.body:
CLEVELAND -- For the third consecutive game, quarterback Deshaun Watson led a winning drive for the Cleveland Browns.

Four days after he threw for the winning score in Cleveland's Week 3 home win over the Carolina Panthers, Watson led the Browns on another late-game drive. This time, he put the Browns in range for Andre Szmyt's 56-yard field goal with 10 seconds left as Cleveland defeated the Pittsburgh Steelers 27-24 on Thursday night.

Watson joined Brian Sipe as the second Browns quarterback since the 1970 merger to lead a winning drive in the fourth quarter or overtime of three straight games, according to ESPN Research.

"It was electric. It was amazing," Watson said. "From the time we came out pregame, it was super dope to be called out, hear the crowd and feel the energy. From start to finish, the crowd was in it, the energy of the stadium, we fed off them. To get a big victory against a divisional rival on primetime, this [is] what you dream about. This is what you work for. These are the things that you put that grind in during the summertime and training camp for nights like this. It was amazing."

The victory, Cleveland's third straight after a 24-point road loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 1, gave the Browns their first 3-1 start since 2021 and moved them into sole possession of the AFC North for the first time since Nov. 9, 2014.

Late turnarounds after slow starts defined Watson's previous two winning drives. But on Thursday night, Watson had one of his best first halves in a Browns uniform. Watson threw for 181 yards, his most in the first half of a game in Cleveland, as the offense scored touchdowns on three consecutive drives in the second quarter. The Browns led 21-10 at halftime, and their 21 points in the second quarter were their most in any quarter of a game since the 2020 wild-card round, also against the Steelers.

The offense stalled for much of the second half, though, and a pair of turnovers from Watson played a role in Pittsburgh being able to erase the deficit. He was stripped in the third quarter by edge rusher T.J. Watt on a rush attempt, and the Steelers recovered. Watson was also intercepted early in the fourth quarter on a pass that was tipped. Pittsburgh scored a touchdown after the giveaway but failed on the 2-point attempt, cutting the Browns' lead to 21-16 with 10:10 remaining.

The Steelers tied the score at 24-24 on a 3-yard touchdown pass from Aaron Rodgers to tight end Pat Freiermuth and a successful 2-point try on a 1-yard sneak by Rodgers after defensive end Jared Verse was flagged for being offsides.

Watson, though, quickly drove the Browns down the field with four straight completions. He was sacked for a 4-yard loss two plays before the winning kick, but he was already within Szmyt's range.

Safety Grant Delpit intercepted a desperation heave from Rodgers to preserve the victory.

articles.headline: Steelers' McCarthy regrets angry exchange with Rodgers in loss
articles.description: Steelers coach Mike McCarthy said he regretted directing a profanity toward quarterback Aaron Rodgers during a heated exchange that was caught on the broadcast of Thursday's 27-24 loss to the Browns.
articles.headlineJa: スティーラーズのマッカーシー監督、敗戦でのロジャースとの激しい口論を後悔
articles.descriptionJa: スティーラーズのミッチ・マッカーシー監督は、木曜日のブラウンズ戦（27-24で敗戦）の中継で捉えられたクォーターバックのアーロン・ロジャースとの激しい口論の中で、暴言を吐いたことを後悔していると述べた。
articles.body:
CLEVELAND -- Steelers coach Mike McCarthy expressed regret for profanity he used toward quarterback Aaron Rodgers that was caught on the broadcast of Pittsburgh's 27-24 loss to the Cleveland Browns on Thursday night.

Midway through the first quarter, a hot mic caught a frustrated Rodgers gesturing and yelling toward the sideline, "What the f---? Call it!" The cameras then cut to McCarthy, who appeared to be upset and muttered a profanity.

"Communication sometimes is not the best choice of words, but everybody's competing on the field," McCarthy said. "I think what's said on the field, the way I grew up in this game, usually stays on the field. That's not the case today. I understand that. But any negative communication on my part, I wish I wouldn't use those words."

McCarthy described the team's first series, one that ended in a 12-yard Roman Wilson touchdown, as "hectic" and added that he was "talking fast, more than normal."

Rodgers said the crowd noise made it difficult to communicate at times.

"It was loud," Rodgers said. "It was definitely a good crowd tonight. It was loud. So some of the calls, it was hard to hear for sure."

Though just the first-quarter exchange was caught on a hot mic, Rodgers expressed frustration and exasperation as he came off the field throughout the night. While the Steelers' nine-minute, 48-second opening drive -- their longest of the season -- ended with a score, the offense stagnated in the second and third quarters.

"It's pretty deflating," tight end Pat Freiermuth said of the Steelers' inability to carry over the offensive momentum to the second quarter. "Wish we were able to continue to move the ball on offense, put our defense in better situations."

Rodgers threw an interception to end the Steelers' second drive after four plays, and the Browns turned it into a touchdown four plays later. While the Browns scored 21 straight points, the Steelers' next six possessions gained just 101 yards and ended with four punts, a missed field goal and a made field goal.

"It wasn't our cleanest game all the way around," Rodgers said. "They're a good defense, so you got to give them credit, but they were getting after us on some of the long-yarded stuff that we weren't winning a bunch, and I missed a couple throws that I usually hit."

But Rodgers and the offense put together a furious fourth-quarter comeback with two touchdowns and a Rodgers quarterback sneak for the 2-point conversion to tie the score with less than two minutes to play. The Browns, though, responded by driving into field goal territory and kicking a 56-yard game winner.

Rodgers completed 22 of 40 attempts for 299 yards, but he was hit 10 times, including five sacks, and threw two interceptions. Each of the sacks came as Rodgers faced man defense. Rodgers has been sacked an NFL-worst 12 times against man defense, seven more than any quarterback this season, according to ESPN Research.

articles.body:
Tomás Araújo is subject to interest from Manchester United and Chelsea, while free agent Jadon Sancho is happy to wait to sign for a club.

Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Manchester United and Chelsea are monitoring a deal for Benfica defender Tomás Araújo, according to TEAMTalk. The 24-year-old is claimed to be on the radar of several Premier League clubs, but it's United and Chelsea who are most keen. Araujo, who can play center back and right-back, recently signed a contract extension until 2031, making an exit in January unlikely. However, with a release clause valued at £68 million, clubs could pursue a switch anyway

- Jadon Sancho is willing to hold out until January as a free agent before making a decision, if the right offer doesn't arrive before then, reports TEAMtalk. The former Manchester United and Borussia Dortmund winger is a free agent, following his exit from Old Trafford at the end of his contract in the summer. The 26-year-old has been linked with a whole host of clubs since, but is yet to make a decision on his future, with nothing advanced on his next club.

- Juventus are preparing a huge rebuild over the next year, with Tuttosport naming a whole host of potential transfer targets for the Italian club. In the goalkeeping ranks, Alisson Becker is claimed to be a player of interest, as he could leave Liverpool at the end of the season as a free agent. In defence, Oumar Solet of Udinese is viewed as an option, while RB Leipzig ace David Raum and Crystal Palace star Tyrick Mitchell are also on the Bianconeri's radar. Napoli stalwart Stanislav Lobotka, Manchester City midfielder Mateo Kovacic, and Real Madrid playmaker Brahim Díaz are touted as options for the central ranks. Meanwhile, Crystal Palace forward Jean-Philippe Mateta could be a striker arrival.

- João Félix is keen on making a return to Barcelona next year, when the Portuguese international's contract with Al Nassr is set to expire. That's according to Sport, which reports that the 27-year-old has his sights set on a return to the Champions League after a recent resurgence in his career in the Saudi Pro League. Felix previously spent a year on loan with Barcelona from Atletico Madrid, where he made 44 appearances with 10 goals and six assists. Now back in form, and eyeing a possible free transfer, a return to the Nou Camp is on his mind, though the report claims that he is not viewed as a priority target.

- Juventus have declared that Kenan Yildiz and Kerim Alajbegovic are "untouchable" in future transfer markets, with the club keen to build around the pair, reports La Gazzetta. Yildiz, 21, has previously attracted interest from Arsenal and Real Madrid, having shown plenty of potential. articles.headline: Ranking the top 10 Premier League's summer transfers so far
articles.description: Which players have impressed since making a move over the summer? Sometimes a £17 million arrival does better than a £117 million one.
articles.headlineJa: ここまでのプレミアリーグ今夏移籍トップ10ランキング
articles.descriptionJa: 今夏の移籍以降、活躍を見せているのはどの選手か？時に1,700万ポンドで加入した選手が、1億1,700万ポンドの選手以上の成果を上げることもある。
articles.body:
We're just five Premier League games, plus a handful of cup bouts across several competitions, into this fledgling 2026-27 campaign. It's too early to hand down definitive verdicts on the slew of players who moved over the course of yet another big-spending summer, but we can take an early look at which players have settled in quickly and impressed the most at their new clubs.

Here's a top 10, ranked on their overall impact and excellence, taking into account every game they've played so far this term, regardless of competition.

10. Ronald Araújo, RB/CB, Liverpool

Key stat: Liverpool are yet to concede in the league with Araújo on the pitch.

Liverpool have won four of their past five games in all competitions, a jump in form that roughly coincides with Araújo entering the XI. He felt like an opportunistic loan signing from Barcelona (with a €55 million permanent option for next summer) that could go one of two distinct ways, but so far he has been an overwhelming positive.

He has the physique and athleticism to survive the rough-and-tumble of the Premier League, while he's also aware enough of his technical limitations to keep his time on the ball simple, accurate and therefore effective -- except for that sumptuous backheel assist for Dominik Szoboszlai's goal against Atlético Madrid, of course.

9. Christos Tzolis, FW, Arsenal

Key stat: He leads Arsenal in assists in all competitions (four).

Tzolis has brought something different to Arsenal's attack. OK, he wasn't the big-name addition (like Vinícius Júnior or Morgan Rogers) the club craved over the summer, but he has been effective from the start.

His debut in the Community Shield brought two assists, and in general the Greece international winger has added a greater connectivity to the left side as he cuts inside onto his right foot. It hasn't all been positive -- he was poor against Brighton & Hove Albion and taken off at halftime against Aston Villa -- but he has comfortably outperformed his €40 million transfer fee so far.

8. Zion Suzuki, GK, Aston Villa

Key stat: He leads the Premier League in goalkeeper sweeps (7).

Emiliano Martínez's exit from Aston Villa to Chelsea caused plenty of concern among the fans, as he is the club's greatest-ever goalkeeper, but from the moment his replacement Suzuki took to the pitch, those concerns were allayed.

The Japan international possesses a fine combination of smart reflexes and a strong physique, allowing him to fling himself across goal to stop shots and claim crosses among the crowd. His eagerness to race out of his box and sweep up has also stood out among his peers.

But the real story with Suzuki is his incredible distribution. He's not only comfortable with the ball at his feet, he's capable of firing off inch-perfect long passes with both feet to spark counterattacks. The early signs are that Villa have replaced Martínez extremely well.

articles.headline: Which Premier League players got injured in the international break?
articles.description: All the latest news and updates on Premier League stars injuries during the first international break of the 2026-2027 club season
articles.headlineJa: 国際試合期間中に負傷したプレミアリーグの選手は？
articles.descriptionJa: 2026-2027クラブシーズンの最初の国際試合中断期間中に負傷したプレミアリーグのスター選手に関する最新ニュースと更新情報。
articles.body:
Premier League teams will be watching and hoping their star players remain healthy throughout the international break.

However, some have already sustained injuries while playing for their countries. Premier League matches resume on Oct. 10.

ESPN will be tracking the latest injuries and updates for your club's players:

Kai Havertz (Arsenal)

Arsenal's Kai Havertz was forced off in the 30th minute of the game between Netherlands and Germany on September 24th with what was described as a muscle injury.

"Both are currently undergoing an MRI," Jurgen Klopp said on RTL about Havertz and Jamal Musiala. "I hope we get the diagnosis [on Thursday] evening. But of course, this isn't great. I hope it's nothing serious. The lads are probably out for us. But hopefully, they'll be back in action relatively quickly."

On September 25 the German Football Association confirmed the attacker would be leaving Klopp's camp and return to Arsenal after suffering what they describe as a 'muscle strain.'

Brian Brobbey (Sunderland)

The powerful Sunderland attacker was also injured in the same game after picking up what looked like a hamstring injury while running for the ball. He immediately went down and signalled to the sideline.

He left the field of his own accord but did have a heavy limp as he walked down the tunnel.

Netherlands boss Xavi Hernandez said after the game: "Brian is indeed injured."

Brobbey was replaced by Joshua Zirkzee in the Dutch squad.

Zion Suzuki (Aston Villa)

The goalkeeper linked up with the Japan squad but according to reports missed the main group training session on September 22nd, according to local reports. Instead he was put on an individual session for a rib injury.

Suzuki was subsequently left out of Japan's matchday squad entirely for Thursday's 3-1 victory over Uruguay.

Dan Ballard (Sunderland)

The Sunderland defender suffered a reported hamstring injury during Northern Ireland's 1-0 victory over Georgia in the UEFA Nations League.

With the score still 0-0 as the match moved into stoppage time, Ballard chased back as Georgia counter-attacked and pulled up clutching the back of his thigh, unable to finish the match in Tbilisi.

Speaking immediately after Friday's match, manager Michael O'Neill said it was too soon to know the extent of his latest injury but will definitely miss the next three Northern Ireland games.

"We'll scan him tomorrow (Saturday), but he's certainly not going to be available for the next three games."

Alexander Isak (Liverpool)

Alexander Isak is returning to Liverpool after sustaining a "minor injury" on international duty.

The striker scored and played the full 90 minutes in Sweden's 2-1 victory over Romania in the Nations League on Friday.

But Isak, who has made a strong start to the season for Liverpool, will not feature in matches against Poland, Bosnia and Herzegovina and Romania over the remainder of the extended international break.

articles.headline: Aaron Rodgers' 2026 NFL season: Tracking records, milestones
articles.description: The Steelers QB is chasing records in his 22nd NFL season, and ESPN is chronicling his "last rodeo."
articles.headlineJa: アーロン・ロジャースの2026年NFLシーズン：記録とマイルストーンを追跡
articles.descriptionJa: NFL22年目のシーズンで記録達成を目指すスティーラーズのQB。ESPNは彼の「ラストロデオ（最後の挑戦）」を記録している。
articles.body:
Entering his 22nd NFL season -- or as Aaron Rodgers says, "his last rodeo" -- the 42-year-old Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback is on the cusp of joining several exclusive clubs as he moves up the ranks in the league record books.

In 2025, he passed former teammate Brett Favre to take sole possession of fourth place in career touchdown passes thrown with his 509th TD pass in the Week 3 win against the New England Patriots.

"Every now and then I made some special throws that led to touchdowns, but I've been playing a long time, and it's a longevity thing," Rodgers said before passing Favre's mark last season. "I'm proud of it, but not a big deal."

Rodgers also went on to supplant Ben Roethlisberger for fifth in all-time passing yards in the second quarter of the Thursday night loss to the Cincinnati Bengals on Oct. 16, 2025.

But now, Rodgers is closing in on his final opportunities to add to that growing list of historic accomplishments.

Among the milestones in reach for Rodgers are becoming the fourth quarterback in NFL history to appear in 300 games (as of Week 3 he has appeared in 290), joining Tom Brady (383), Favre (326) and Drew Brees (305), throwing the fourth-most touchdown passes in NFL history (as of Week 3, he has 531) and having the second-most regular-season games with multiple touchdown passes. And after Week 3, he needs 3,026 yards to become the fifth player to reach 70,000 passing yards. 

This season, we're chronicling Rodgers' individual milestones week by week as he rides his last rodeo. Follow along here for the weekly installments.

Preseason: 0-for-0, 0 yards, 0 INT, 0 sacks, 0 rushes

Despite early hints that Rodgers would take the field during the Steelers' first preseason under McCarthy, the veteran quarterback instead spent two games on the sideline and one on his couch at home. With Rodgers' top two receivers in DK Metcalf and Michael Pittman Jr. sidelined with preseason injuries, McCarthy opted to also keep his quarterback under wraps.

Rodgers isn't a stranger to sitting out the preseason in recent years. He didn't play in any preseason games for the Steelers in 2025, nor for the New York Jets in 2024 following his season-ending left Achilles tear in Week 1 of the 2023 season.

Week 1: Steelers 20, Falcons 13

Rodgers' stat line: 221 yards, 1 TD, 0 INTs, 2 sacks, 3 rushes for -1 yard

Rodgers didn't break any records this week, but he pulled within one touchdown pass of Peyton Manning for fourth most in NFL history with his second-quarter throw to tight end Pat Freiermuth for 6 yards. The touchdown toss was Rodgers' 232nd of the regular season. Rodgers had 26 pass attempts in the first half, his most attempts in the first half of a game since 2020 at Minnesota as a member of the Green Bay Packers, per ESPN Research.

After Sunday's game, coach Mike McCarthy said he wanted to find more balance in his offense, which ran the ball just 21 times to Rodgers' 40 pass attempts. Rodgers, though, didn't mind all the throwing.

articles.headline: Browns best Steelers on TNF to take lead in AFC North
articles.description: The Browns move to 3-1 while adding to Pittsburgh's historic five-year futility in Cleveland.
articles.headlineJa: ブラウンズがTNFでスティーラーズを破りAFC北地区首位に立つ
articles.descriptionJa: ブラウンズは3勝1敗とし、クリーブランドにおけるピッツバーグの5年間に及ぶ歴史的な不振をさらに更新させた。
articles.body:
CLEVELAND -- After losing hold of an 11-point lead in the fourth quarter, Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson delivered a late-game performance again Thursday night. Andre Szmyt made a 56-yard field goal with 10 seconds and safety Grant Delpit intercepted a last-second heave from quarterback Aaron Rodgers as the Browns defeated the Pittsburgh Steelers in a 27-24 win.

The victory marks the first time the Browns have sat atop the division since Nov. 9, 2014. It's also Cleveland's first 3-1 start since the 2021 season.

After the offense struggled in the first half of the team's first three games, the unit broke out with three consecutive touchdown drives in the second quarter to give the Browns a 21-10 lead at halftime.

Cleveland's offense stalled in the second half, as Watson turned the ball over twice, but the starting QB, who entered Week 4 with two straight game-winning drives, led his third of the young season.

Watson completed 24 of 33 passes for 268 yards with one touchdown and an interception. He also ran for 22 yards on seven carries and lost a fumble.

After running for a combined 131 yards in the season's first two games, the Browns ran for 112 yards Thursday night, the second time the team has had back-to-back 100-yard rushing efforts.

Cleveland's defense sacked Rodgers five times and intercepted him twice.

Cleveland Browns (3-1)

What to make of the QB performance: Watson started off strong before cooling off in the second half and turning it on late again. Watson's 181 passing yards were the most he has thrown for in the first half of a game since joining the Browns, but his two turnovers after halftime helped Pittsburgh erase the deficit. Watson, though, was clutch for the third straight game, building on his early-season momentum.

Stat to know: The Browns scored 21 points in the first half, their most in any half of a game since Week 8 of the 2024 season, when Cleveland scored 23 points against the Baltimore Ravens in the second half.

Trend to watch: Cleveland was flagged for 17 total penalties, the second straight game with at least 14 infractions. Entering Week 4, the Browns had been called for the second-most penalties in the NFL (34).

Best quote out of the locker room: "This isn't the old Browns. We've got new swag. We're a lot more aggressive, getting after it. This is something different here. We're going to make this whole city rock," said Browns defensive end Jared Verse. -- Daniel Oyefusi
